verdict.rationale: Gumloop documents agents that pursue goals on their own and can be run without a user present. Runs can be started by recurring or one-time schedules, by app triggers when something happens in an external service, and by webhook URLs, and a Performance view shows what an agent has been doing. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that background scheduled and triggered runs work reliably in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Schedule your agent to run automatically on a recurring schedule or as a one-time trigger.

Set up scheduled triggers to run on a recurring or one-time basis, app triggers to fire when something happens in an external service, or a webhook trigger to fire when another app sends data to a unique URL.
Build AI agents that use your tools and data to do real work, then automate them with triggers, schedules, and the API.
You give an agent a goal and a set of tools, and it figures out how to get there: which tools to call, in what order, and when to ask you for input.
A webhook trigger gives an agent its own URL.
what is it costing, is it doing good work, and what has it actually been doing.
